exercise.name: Dumbbell Windmill

reference.title: Dumbbell Standing Windmill
reference.listing: Animated GIF; data sheet: body part Waist, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength

exercise.mechanics: Compound (hip hinge with trunk side-bend and rotation under an overhead load)

breathing.pattern: Inhale and brace before you hinge; breathe out as you stand back up.
breathing.cadence: About 2.4 s down, a short pause, about 2.4 s up

prescription.tempo: Slow: about 2-3 s down, brief pause, 2-3 s up
prescription.progression: Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight that leaves about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8) at the end of each set. Learn it with no weight or a light dumbbell first; add load only when the arm stays vertical and the eyes stay on the weight.

cues.text: Feet wider than the hips, both feet turned about 45 degrees to the left. Press the dumbbell overhead in the right hand and lock the elbow; eyes on the dumbbell.
Push the right hip out and back, then hinge and side-bend to the left; slide the left hand down the inside of the left leg.
Pause with the left hand near the shin: right arm vertical, chest open toward the dumbbell, right knee straight, left knee soft.
Drive the hips forward and stand back up the same path, eyes still on the dumbbell.
Stand tall with the arm locked; finish the set, then switch sides.

mistakes.mistake: The overhead arm drifting forward or bending
mistakes.fix: Keep the knuckles to the ceiling and the arm stacked over the shoulder; go lighter.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding forward instead of hinging at the hips
mistakes.fix: Push the right hip back first; the spine stays long.

mistakes.mistake: Reaching for the floor with the left hand
mistakes.fix: Go only as low as you can with the arm vertical; mid-shin is plenty.
Eyes on the dumbbell for the whole rep.

kinematics.norm: Hip hinge with a side-bend and an open chest; no study defines the angles (clinical opinion)
The loaded-side knee straight, the other soft; the hips hinge (clinical opinion)
Slides down the inside of the front leg toward the shin or foot (clinical opinion)
Wider than the hips, turned about 45 degrees away from the dumbbell (clinical opinion)
Slow and controlled, about 2-3 s each way (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #490113, Dumbbell Standing Windmill, animated gif (movement reference)
Konrad, Schmitz and Denner 2001, neuromuscular evaluation of trunk-training exercises (J Athl Train 36(2):109-118; PMC155519)
McGill, Juker and Kropf, quantitative intramuscular myoelectric activity of quadratus lumborum during a wide variety of tasks (Clinical Biomechanics)
McGill 1998, low back exercises: evidence for improving exercise regimens (Phys Ther 78(7):754-765; PMID 9672547)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Choose a dumbbell load you can control for every rep; the load is user-chosen.
Shoulder pain, instability or limited overhead mobility: do not hold a weight overhead; practise the hinge with no load or a low windmill.
Low-back pain: keep the range small; the hinge and side-bend combine under load.
Never let the dumbbell drift over the head; if the arm wavers, bring the weight down and end the set.
modify: No weight (bodyweight windmill) or the free hand on a box to shorten the range.
Dumbbell held low in the free hand instead (low windmill).

muscleNotes.obliques_r: The obliques on the dumbbell side lower the trunk into the side-bend under control and pull it back up; side-lying lateral flexion work drove external oblique to about 98% MVC in Konrad 2001. No EMG study of the windmill was found (clinical opinion for the windmill itself).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Quadratus lumborum and the erector spinae on the dumbbell side hold the trunk as it hinges and bends; quadratus lumborum is a primary lateral stabiliser (McGill, Juker and Kropf).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Both glutes control the hip hinge and drive the stand-up, the right hip pushed back and out (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Both glutes control the hip hinge and drive the stand-up, the right hip pushed back and out (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: The obliques on the free-hand side turn the chest open toward the dumbbell (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Steadies the pelvis over the planted feet as the hips shift (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Steadies the pelvis over the planted feet as the hips shift (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Lengthen as the hips hinge over the nearly straight right leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Lengthen as the hips hinge over the nearly straight right leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis and the deep abdominals keep the trunk braced (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Holds the arm locked vertical overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Holds the arm locked vertical overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Keeps the shoulder blade rotated up under the load (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff centres the shoulder as the trunk turns under the fixed arm (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Supports the shoulder girdle under the overhead load (clinical opinion).

guides.label: Free hand slides down the leg
Dumbbell stays stacked over the shoulder
